findings.text: The first paragraph does its job. A newcomer learns what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves before reading anything else.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The second section is an error message. The opening says Athena records the models, cost and verdict, but the one place meant to show this on a real job shows nothing. That weakens the pitch right where a newcomer would look for proof.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: The page is Athena's site, but nearly all of it explains firstmate, a different project. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena has to read past twelve transition cards, exit codes and 45 claims before reaching the steps for Athena itself.
findings.source: <title>Athena explains how firstmate handles work</title>, and the sections from "Start here" to "Claims and sources"

findings.text: The page does say why it shows firstmate: it is a worked example. But it never connects that example back to the main pitch, which is turning a one-line request into a commit. A newcomer may not see how this study shows that.
findings.source: "A study is Athena's written reading of another software project... Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it"

findings.text: The next steps are concrete and complete: prerequisites, clone, install and a first command. A link near the top jumps straight to them.
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" / "./setup.sh" / "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: Some text is for the repository owner, not a visitor. Placed in the header, this link may make a newcomer wonder whether the page was meant for them.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision." and About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from"

findings.text: Several glossary entries say only that the term is undefined. This is honest, but a newcomer still does not learn what the word means.
findings.source: Glossary entries for captain call, durable record, endpoint, heartbeat, wake: "The firstmate source does not define..."

findings.text: The same rules are repeated across many sections, which makes a long page longer. A newcomer skimming for the main point has to read the same sentences several times.
findings.source: The yolo/red rule is stated under "Words used first", "What firstmate is", "One piece of work", "When things go wrong", card t10 and the Glossary
